jordan.p: Heads-up from today's int4v2 onboarding of arcus-30b. I hit a deterministic wraparound glitch on resume past 16k tokens that looks like RoPE index reset instead of continuous tiling. Repro + logs below.

liam.s: repro command?

jordan.p: minimal (dedicated, int4v2, no shard-swap):
```bash
./bench-run --model arcus-30b:2026-03 --quant int4v2 --context 16384 \\n  --resume-checkpoint ckpt_20260320 --user tests/very_long_dialog.txt \\n  --rope-rescale=auto --kv-chunk-size=4096 --no-shard-swap
```

rachel: what failure mode do you see? null output or wrong tokens?

jordan.p: not null, but tokens after resume start repeating a previous segment ~512 tokens later. Baseline fp16 and int8 do not show this. Logs: 
```
[RESUME] checkpoint_pos=16384 attach_base=15360
[ATTN] prev_idx=16299 pos_scaled=16299 rot_phase=0x1a
[ATTN] next_idx=64 pos_scaled=64 rot_phase=0x1a  # wrap expected but base should be 16384+64 not 64
[KV] kv_slot=64 mapped_to=16384  # mapping inconsistent
```

liam.s: that mapping looks like we applied modulo without adding the resume base. Could be memcpy windowing that zeroes top bits on int4v2 memcpy kernel.

bench-bot: run 5055550000 queued (bench-suite: int4v2/arcus-onboard)

jordan.p: I toggled `--rope-rescale=none` vs `auto` and also tried `--kv-chunk-size=8192`. Changing chunk size moves the point where repetition occurs (consistent with a chunk alignment bug).

rachel: can you try forcing a manual kv_rebase on resume? `--kv-force-rebase=true`?

jordan.p: `--kv-force-rebase=true` removes the repeat but increases RT latency ~12%. Confirms the delta application path is wrong.

liam.s: action items: 1) add micro unit test that simulates a resume at boundary (context=16384) with int4v2 memcpy path enabled; 2) compare memcpy outputs between fp16 path and int4v2 path for the same kv region; 3) audit any code that compresses index into 16-bit slots (possible truncation). I'll take 2+3.

jordan.p: ran a quick quant-quality sweep across 3 seeds (BLEU vs fp16): fp16=1.0, int8=0.995, int4v1=0.93, int4v2=0.948. int4v2 better but still shows resume issue.

rachel: good that int4v2 is improved for steady-state, but we need correctness on resume. Could be a packing/stride off-by-one in the new kernel.

jordan.p: opened PR 4999 with failing unit and trace: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4999

ci-bot: PR 4999  CI started (unit: kv_resume_boundary_test)

liam.s: I'll try to repro locally with cuda-memcheck and run the int4v2 memcpy kernel under different alignments. If I can reproduce in unit, I'll bisect kernel change.

rachel: for release checklist, add "resume boundary smoke under quant kernels" and include a tiny text file that reproduces in <30s.

jordan.p: noted. Also documenting: observed behavior only when `--rope-rescale=auto` interacts with resume; setting `none` hides but doesn't fix underlying mapping. Putting details in PR description.

liam.s: thanks. If anyone sees related issues on dedicated canary, drop logs here. We'll coordinate landing fix and follow-up canary runs.

jordan.p: thanks all."
